questions.question: What is the full form of CD, commonly used in storage devices?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Compact Disc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **CD** stands for **Compact Disc**, which is a digital optical disc storage format.
 
• It was originally developed by **Philips** and **Sony** in 1982 for storing and playing music.
 
• Compact Discs are used for storing various types of digital data, including **audio, video, and software programs**.
 
• A standard CD has a storage capacity of approximately **700 MB** or 80 minutes of audio.
 
• CDs use a **laser to read data** encoded in the form of tiny indentations (pits) on the disc surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of CDs**

 
 
• The first commercial Compact Disc was released in **1982** and featured the album "52nd Street" by Billy Joel.
 
• CD technology revolutionized how music and data were stored and distributed during the 1980s and 1990s.
 
 
 
• **Types of CDs**
 
 
• **CD-ROM**: Read-only memory discs used for data storage.
 
• **CD-R**: Recordable discs that allow data to be written once.
 
• **CD-RW**: Rewritable discs that allow data to be erased and rewritten multiple times.
 
 
 
• **How CDs Work**
 
 
• Data is stored in the form of microscopic pits and lands on the reflective surface of the disc.
 
• A laser beam reads the data by detecting changes in reflection caused by pits and lands.
 
 
 
• **Decline of CDs**
 
 
• With the rise of **USB drives, cloud storage, and streaming platforms**, CDs have become less popular.
 
• However, they are still used in some industries and for **archival purposes**.

questions.question: The title name 'Rani Gaidinliu' was given to the Naga revolt leader Gaidinliu Pamei by which political leader?

questions.question: Indira Point, the southernmost tip of India, is located on which island?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Great Nicobar Island**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indira Point is the southernmost tip of India, located on **Great Nicobar Island** in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• It is situated at **6°45'10" N latitude** and **93°49'36" E longitude**, making it the southernmost geographical point of India.
 
• Indira Point was formerly known as **Pygmalion Point** before being renamed in honor of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• The location was significantly affected by the **2004 Indian Ocean tsunami**, which caused submersion of parts of the area.
 
• Great Nicobar Island is the largest island in the Nicobar group and is home to the **Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve**, known for its rich biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nicobar Islands:**

 
 
• The Nicobar Islands are part of the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, located in the Indian Ocean.
 
• They consist of 22 islands divided into three groups: North Nicobar, Central Nicobar, and South Nicobar.
 
• The indigenous communities residing here include the **Nicotanese** and **Shompen tribes**.
 
 
 
• **2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami:**
 
 
• The tsunami was triggered by a massive earthquake off the coast of Sumatra, Indonesia, measuring **9.1-9.3 on the Richter scale**.
 
• It caused widespread destruction across coastal regions, including Indira Point, where the land submerged partially.
 
• Great Nicobar Island was one of the worst-hit areas, leading to loss of lives and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• It is a UNESCO-designated biosphere reserve, known for its unique flora and fauna.
 
• Species like **saltwater crocodiles, Nicobar megapodes, and leatherback turtles** are found here.
 
• Efforts are being undertaken to conserve the biodiversity of this region.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• Great Nicobar Island has strategic importance due to its proximity to the Strait of Malacca, a key maritime trade route.
 
• India is developing infrastructure projects like the **Nicobar Transshipment Port** to enhance its presence in the region.

questions.question: Which Princely State had a representative assembly from as early as 1881?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mysore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The princely state of **Mysore** was one of the progressive states in British India and introduced a representative assembly as early as **1881**.
 
• The assembly was established under the reign of Maharaja **Chamarajendra Wadiyar X** to provide limited representation to the people.
 
• This was an important step towards constitutional governance and public involvement in administration in princely states.
 
• The Mysore Representative Assembly was one of the **earliest examples of democratic institutions** within a princely state during British rule.
 
• The assembly primarily acted as an advisory body and discussed matters related to the administration of the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Princely States in British India**:

 
 
• India had over 500 princely states during British rule, which were governed by local rulers but under British suzerainty.
 
• The princely states had varying levels of autonomy in administration and governance.
 
• Mysore was among the most advanced princely states in terms of governance and infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Mysore's Progressive Policies**:
 
 
• Mysore is known for its early emphasis on education, industrialization, and public welfare.
 
• The establishment of representative institutions reflected the state's commitment to modernization.
 
 
 
• **Role of Representative Assemblies**:
 
 
• Representative assemblies in princely states acted as consultative bodies, advising rulers on matters of public interest.
 
• They were early experiments in democratic governance, paving the way for modern legislative structures.
 
 
 
• **Chamarajendra Wadiyar X**:
 
 
• He was the ruler of Mysore from 1868 to 1894 and played a key role in modernizing the state.
 
• Under his reign, Mysore saw significant advancements in governance and infrastructure.

Find the **cumulative frequencies**: 23, 36, 60, 85, 120.

Total items **N** = 120, so **N/2** = 60.

The cumulative frequency 60 corresponds exactly to the **upper limit** of the class 240−290.

When **N/2** exactly matches a cumulative frequency, the **Median** is that class boundary.

**∴ The correct answer is 290.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Classes:** 140−190, 190−240, 240−290, 290−340, 340−390

**Frequencies (f):** 23, 13, 24, 25, 35

**Cumulative Frequencies (cf):** 23, 36, 60, 85, 120

**Formula Used:**

**Median** = L + [((N/2) − cfₚ) ÷ f] × h

Where **L** = lower limit of median class, **N** = total frequency, **cfₚ** = cumulative frequency of the preceding class, **f** = frequency of the median class, **h** = class width.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total frequency **N** = 120

⇒ **N/2** = 120 ÷ 2 = 60

⇒ The cumulative frequency just greater than or equal to 60 is 60 (Class 240−290).

⇒ **L** = 240, **cfₚ** = 36, **f** = 24, **h** = 50

⇒ Median = 240 + [(60 − 36) ÷ 24] × 50

⇒ Median = 240 + [24 ÷ 24] × 50

⇒ Median = 240 + 1 × 50

⇒ Median = 240 + 50

⇒ Median = 290

**∴ The correct answer is 290.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between central tendencies is given by: **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**.

Class Mark

Mean for Grouped Data

The arithmetic **Mean** (μ) is calculated using Σfx ÷ Σf, where x is the class mark and f is the frequency.</p

questions.question: For a regular polygon, the sum of the interior angles is 50% more than the sum of its exterior angles. Each interior angle of the polygon measures x°. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The sum of all exterior angles of any regular polygon is always **360°**.

Sum of interior angles = 360° + 50% of 360° = 360° + 180° = **540°**.

The polygon with a sum of interior angles equal to 540° is a regular **pentagon** (5 sides).

Each interior angle (x) of a regular pentagon = 540° ÷ 5 = **108°**.

**∴ The correct answer is 108°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of interior angles = Sum of exterior angles + 50% of Sum of exterior angles

Each interior angle = x°

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon = (n − 2) × 180°

Sum of exterior angles of any polygon = 360°

Each interior angle of a regular polygon = [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b5297a6f8726282088ad796190e3e68d0deb7541d4e296db322009cfa84360f3.png] 

Let the number of sides of the regular polygon be **n**.

The sum of the exterior angles of any polygon is always **360°**.

According to the question, the sum of the interior angles is 50% more than the sum of its exterior angles:

⇒ Sum of interior angles = 360° + 50% of 360°

⇒ Sum of interior angles = 360° + 180° = 540°

We know that the sum of the interior angles of an n-sided polygon is given by the formula:

⇒ (n − 2) × 180° = 540°

⇒ n − 2 = 540° ÷ 180°

⇒ n − 2 = 3

⇒ n = 5

Thus, the polygon is a regular **pentagon** (n = 5).

Each interior angle of a regular polygon is given by:

⇒ x = [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n

⇒ x = (3 × 180°) ÷ 5

⇒ x = 540° ÷ 5

⇒ x = 108°

**Why other options are incorrect:**

⇒ **Option (2) 96°:** If each interior angle is 96°, then the number of sides n = 360° ÷ (180° − 96°) = 360° ÷ 84° = 4.28, which is not an integer.

⇒ **Option (3) 112°:** If each interior angle is 112°, then the number of sides n = 360° ÷ (180° − 112°) = 360° ÷ 68° = 5.29, which is not an integer.

⇒ **Option (4) 88°:** If each interior angle is 88°, then the number of sides n = 360° ÷ (180° − 88°) = 360° ÷ 92° = 3.91, which is not an integer.

**∴ The correct answer is 108°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of the interior angles of any convex polygon with n sides is always (n − 2) × 180°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon is always 360°, regardless of the number of sides.

Interior and Exterior Angle Relationship

At any vertex of a polygon, the interior angle and the exterior angle are supplementary, meaning their sum is always 180°.</p

questions.question:
Which of the following are the key factors that are favourable for India for making it a key destination for foreign investments?

2. Ongoing structural reforms

3. Decreasing consumer market position
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 2 only**__.

__
 
• **India’s robust economic fundamentals:** India’s GDP growth rate and macroeconomic stability make it an attractive destination for foreign investments.
 
• **Ongoing structural reforms:** Reforms like GST implementation, labour law rationalization, and measures to ease doing business have enhanced India’s investment climate.
 
• **Favorable demographic profile:** India has a young and large workforce, which supports long-term economic growth and consumer demand, further inviting investments.
 
• **Global supply chain diversification:** Amidst geopolitical tensions, India is seen as a favorable alternative to other countries for manufacturing and investments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structural Reforms:** These include direct tax rationalization, banking sector reforms (e.g., Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code), and digitization initiatives like Digital India.
 
• **FDI Liberalization:** India has allowed 100% FDI in several sectors such as telecom, single-brand retail, and construction, boosting investor confidence.
 
• **India’s Consumer Market:** With a rapidly growing middle class, India is one of the world’s largest consumer markets, though the statement "decreasing consumer market position" in option 3 is incorrect.
 
• **Ease of Doing Business:** India’s rank in the World Bank's Ease of Doing Business index has improved significantly due to streamlined processes and policy reforms.
 
• **Geopolitical Factors:** Trade wars and shifts in global supply chains have positioned India as a strategic investment hub for multinational corporations.

questions.question: What was Ashoka's relation to Bindusara?
questions.solution:

• **Chandragupta Maurya:** Ashoka's grandfather, who established the Mauryan Empire in 321 BCE with the assistance of Chanakya, a renowned strategist and philosopher.
 
• **Kalinga War:** The pivotal war fought in 261 BCE, which led to Ashoka's spiritual awakening and his adoption of Buddhism.
 
• **Rock and Pillar Edicts:** Ashoka's inscriptions found across India and neighboring regions, spreading messages of Buddhism, tolerance, and welfare for his subjects.

__

• The report emphasizes that this rate of reduction aligns with the goals of the **Paris Agreement**, which aims to keep global temperature rise well below 2°C and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.
 
• Current policies and pledges fall significantly short, requiring urgent action to bridge the emissions gap and achieve the 1.5°C target.
 
• Key sectors contributing to emissions include energy, industry, transportation, and agriculture, all of which need rapid decarbonization.
 
• Increased investments in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies are vital to achieve these reductions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Paris Agreement:** An international treaty adopted in 2015 to combat climate change and strengthen global responses by limiting global warming to well below 2°C, preferably 1.5°C, above pre-industrial levels.
 
• **Greenhouse Gases (GHGs):** Gases like carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O) that trap heat in the atmosphere and contribute to global warming.
 
• **Carbon Neutrality:** Achieving a balance between emitted carbon dioxide and its removal from the atmosphere, often referred to as "net zero" emissions.
 
• **Renewable Energy:** Sources like solar, wind, and hydropower that produce energy without depleting natural resources or causing significant environmental harm.

questions.question:
Find the circumference (in m) of the largest circle that can be inscribed in a rectangle whose dimensions are given as 112 m and 281 m.

Take pi = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a circle **inscribed** in a **rectangle**, the **diameter** of the **largest circle** is equal to the **smaller side** of the rectangle.

Smaller side (d) = 112 m

Circumference = πd = (22/7) × 112

Circumference = 22 × 16 = 352 m

**∴ The correct answer is 352 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of rectangle (L) = 281 m

Breadth of rectangle (B) = 112 m

**Formula Used:**

Diameter of the **largest inscribed circle** in a rectangle = **Breadth (B)**

Circumference of circle = π × diameter

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c6ac8c3979309067e0ca0decd16508145f218c785faef0bea934f5603bd6627.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Diameter (d) = 112 m

⇒ Radius (r) = d ÷ 2 = 112 ÷ 2 = 56 m

⇒ Circumference = 2 × π × r

⇒ Circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 56

⇒ Circumference = 2 × 22 × 8

⇒ Circumference = 44 × 8 = 352 m

**∴ The correct answer is 352 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Inscribed Circle

The area of the **largest circle** that can be inscribed in a rectangle is π × (B/2)², where B is the **shorter side**.

Circle in a Square

For a **square** of side 'a', the diameter of the **inscribed circle** is exactly 'a', and the diameter of the **circumscribed circle** is a√2.

Circumference and Radius Relations

If the radius is 7 units, the circumference is 44 units and the area is 154 square units. This **ratio** is very useful for fast calculations.</p

questions.question: Nick, Kevin, and Joe can finish a certain piece of work in 3, 9, and 27 days respectively. All three of them started the work together. Nick left after working for 1 day, and Kevin left 2 days before the work was completed. Find the total number of days taken to complete the work.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 3, 9, 27) = 27 units.

Efficiencies: **Nick** = 9, **Kevin** = 3, **Joe** = 1.

Work done in 1st day (all three) = 9 + 3 + 1 = 13 units. Remaining = 14 units.

Since Kevin left 2 days before completion, Joe worked alone for those last 2 days: 2 × 1 = 2 units.

Work left for Kevin and Joe together = 14 − 2 = 12 units. Time taken = 12 ÷ (3 + 1) = 3 days.

Total days = 1 (together) + 3 (Kevin & Joe) + 2 (Joe alone) = 6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 **Nick** 3 27 9 
 **Kevin** 9 3 
 **Joe** 27 1 

Let the **total number of days** to complete the work be **x**.

⇒ Nick worked for 1 day: Work = 9 × 1 = 9 units.

⇒ Kevin worked for (x − 2) days: Work = 3 × (x − 2) units.

⇒ Joe worked for x days: Work = 1 × x = x units.

⇒ Total Work = 9 + 3(x − 2) + x = 27

⇒ 9 + 3x − 6 + x = 27

⇒ 4x + 3 = 27

⇒ 4x = 24

⇒ x = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Leaving Before Completion Trick

If a person leaves 'n' days before completion, add their (n × efficiency) to the total work and divide by the sum of efficiencies of active workers.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each individual, which is (Efficiency × Time).

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work (E ∝ 1/T).</p

questions.question: What positive value of X satisfies the equation(X)/(176) = (99)/(X)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In the equation X/176 = 99/X, **X** is the **mean proportional** between 176 and 99.

Shortcut formula: X = √(a × b)

X = √(176 × 99) = √(11 × 16 × 11 × 9)

X = 11 × 4 × 3 = 132

**∴ The correct answer is 132.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation: (X)/(176) = (99)/(X)

Requirement: Find the **positive value** of X.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b04b38cbf9a15535f8ca512c348e40415e78ccc5c176eec3b20e4ea955914b02.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ X × X = 176 × 99

⇒ X² = 17424

⇒ X = √17424

⇒ X = √(16 × 11 × 9 × 11)

⇒ X = √(16 × 9 × 11²)

⇒ X = 4 × 3 × 11

⇒ X = 132

**∴ The correct answer is 132.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

If three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion such that a/b = b/c, then b is called the mean proportional and b = √(ac).

Cross-Multiplication Rule

For any proportion a/b = c/d, the product of the means equals the product of the extremes: a × d = b × c.

Square Root Extraction

To find the square root of large numbers, factorize them into perfect squares: √(176 × 99) = √(16 × 11 × 9 × 11) = 4 × 3 × 11 = 132.</p

questions.question: Who among the following has the authority to specify an urban area as a 'large urban area' or a 'small urban area' or a 'transitional area' in a state?

options.text: Chief Justice of the State's High Court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor of the State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The authority to specify an urban area as a 'large urban area', 'small urban area', or 'transitional area' in a state is vested with the **Governor of the State**.
 
• This classification is made under the provisions of the **Constitution of India**, specifically Article 243Q.
 
• The Governor acts based on the recommendations of the state government and relevant demographic and administrative factors.
 
• Such classifications are essential for determining governance structures and resource allocation in urban local bodies.
 
• The Governor's decision takes into account criteria such as population density, revenue generation, and infrastructure needs of the area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 243Q:**

 
 
• This article deals with the constitution of municipalities in urban areas.
 
• It mandates the classification of areas into transitional, small, and large urban areas for governance.
 
 
 
• **Urban Local Bodies:**
 
 
• These include municipal corporations, municipalities, and Nagar Panchayats.
 
• The classification helps in determining the appropriate governance model for each type.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Role:**
 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• In matters of urban area classifications, the Governor consults with state authorities for proper implementation.
 
 
 
• **Demographic Considerations:**
 
 
• Population density, infrastructure, and revenue generation are key factors in urban area classification.
 
• Such classifications impact the development plans and funding allocations for urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Urban Governance:**
 
 
• Effective urban governance ensures better resource management and development planning.
 
• It also helps in addressing challenges such as urban poverty, sanitation, and housing.

questions.question: How does the President of India exercise his/her executive functions with respect to decision-making?

options.text: The President considers the advice of the Prime Minister and the Union council of ministers.
The President can repeatedly ask for reconsideration of any ministerial decision until satisfied.
The President acts entirely on his own absolute discretion
The President acts independently of the Union Government for foreign affairs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The President considers the advice of the Prime Minister and the Union council of ministers.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India exercises executive powers based on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Union Council of Ministers as per Article 74 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• While the President has the right to seek information and clarification, he/she cannot act independently of the advice provided by the Council of Ministers.
 
• The President may request the Council of Ministers to reconsider their advice but is bound to act according to the reconsidered advice.
 
• This ensures that the President’s role is largely ceremonial and decisions are aligned with parliamentary democracy principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 74:** Specifies that the President must act according to the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• **Ceremonial Role:** The President’s role is primarily ceremonial, representing the unity and integrity of the nation.
 
• **Reconsideration Power:** The President can return a decision for reconsideration once, but the advice is binding if resubmitted.
 
• **Checks and Balances:** The system ensures that the executive authority remains with the elected representatives while maintaining constitutional decorum.
 
• **Parliamentary Democracy:** India follows a parliamentary system where executive decisions are made by the elected government, not the President.

questions.question: A bank offers 1.1% compound interest per annum calculated on a half-yearly basis. A customer deposits ₹7,745 each on 1 January and 1 July of a year. At the end of the year, the amount he would have gained by way of interest is ________. (Rounded up to the 2 decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate per **half-year** = 1.1% ÷ 2 = 0.55%

1st Deposit (Jan 1) earns interest for **2 periods**: Interest Factor = (1.0055)² − 1 = 0.01103025

2nd Deposit (July 1) earns interest for **1 period**: Interest Factor = 0.0055

Total Interest = ₹7,745 × (0.01103025 + 0.0055) = ₹7,745 × 0.01653025

Total Interest ≈ ₹128.03

**∴ The correct answer is ₹128.03.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Annual Interest Rate = **1.1%** | Compounding = **Half-yearly**

Principal (P₁) on Jan 1 = **₹7,745** | Principal (P₂) on July 1 = **₹7,745**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b35d476511e509da65fa3db0830ea96f9b2359ace284f561d21a517298d67abf.png] 

**Formula:** Interest = P[(1 + r/100)ⁿ − 1]

⇒ Half-yearly rate (r) = 1.1% ÷ 2 = 0.55%

⇒ For the 1st deposit (n = 2 half-years):

⇒ Interest₁ = 7745 × [(1 + 0.55/100)² − 1]

⇒ Interest₁ = 7745 × [(1.0055)² − 1] = 7745 × [1.01103025 − 1] = ₹85.42928...

⇒ For the 2nd deposit (n = 1 half-year):

⇒ Interest₂ = 7745 × [(1 + 0.55/100)¹ − 1]

⇒ Interest₂ = 7745 × 0.0055 = ₹42.5975

⇒ Total Interest = Interest₁ + Interest₂ = 85.42928 + 42.5975 = ₹128.02678...

⇒ Rounded to 2 decimal places = ₹128.03

**∴ The correct answer is ₹128.03.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿt, where A is amount, P is principal, r is annual rate, n is number of compounding periods per year, and t is time in years.

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the annual rate is divided by 2 and the total time (in years) is multiplied by 2.

Effective Annual Rate (EAR)

EAR = (1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1. For 1.1% compounded half-yearly, EAR = (1 + 0.0055)² − 1 ≈ 1.103%.

questions.question: A train P going at the speed of 78 km/hr completely passes train Q of length 120 m, going in the same direction on parallel tracks, at 62 km/hr, in 4.5 minutes. How much time (in seconds) will P take to cross completely train R of length 245 m, going at 81 km/hr in the opposite direction?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative speed** (P and Q) = 78 − 62 = 16 kmph = 16 × (5/18) m/s.

**Total distance** (LP + 120) = Speed × Time = (16 × 5/18) × (4.5 × 60) = 1200 m.

**Length of P** = 1200 − 120 = 1080 m.

**Crossing R**: Speed = 78 + 81 = 159 kmph; Distance = 1080 + 245 = 1325 m.

**Time** = 1325 ÷ (159 × 5/18) = (1325 × 18) ÷ (159 × 5) = 30 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 seconds.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b15b0bcefb5344663c14e7b10e38878cd3c49f4950b8d0435be74204e0bcb585.png] 

**Given:** SpeedP = 78 km/hr, SpeedQ = 62 km/hr, LengthQ = 120 m, TimePQ = 4.5 min. SpeedR = 81 km/hr, LengthR = 245 m.

**Formula:** Relative Speed (Same) = S₁ − S₂ | Relative Speed (Opposite) = S₁ + S₂ | Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Relative speed with Q = 78 − 62 = 16 km/hr = 16 × (5/18) = 40/9 m/s.

⇒ Time = 4.5 × 60 = 270 seconds.

⇒ Total Distance = LP + LQ = (40/9) × 270 = 1200 m.

⇒ LP = 1200 − 120 = 1080 m.

⇒ Relative speed with R = 78 + 81 = 159 km/hr = 159 × (5/18) m/s.

⇒ Total Distance to cross R = 1080 + 245 = 1325 m.

⇒ Required Time = 1325 ÷ (159 × 5 / 18) = (1325 × 18) ÷ 795 = 30 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 seconds.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, subtract their speeds (u − v). When they move in **opposite directions**, add their speeds (u + v).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Distance

When a train crosses another train or a platform, the **total distance** covered is always the **sum of their lengths** (L₁ + L₂).</p

questions.question: What motion is responsible for the generation of waves in a string?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Periodic oscillatory motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Periodic oscillatory motion involves the repetitive back-and-forth movement of an object about a mean position.
 
• This motion causes particles in the string to vibrate, thereby generating mechanical waves.
 
• In the case of a string, periodic oscillation produces transverse waves, where the displacement of the string is perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• Such oscillations are triggered when the string is displaced from its equilibrium position and is subjected to a restoring force, such as tension.
 
• Examples of periodic oscillatory motion include plucking a guitar string, which initiates vibrational waves traveling along the string.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wave Types:** Waves in a string are typically transverse waves, where the oscillation direction is perpendicular to the wave propagation.
 
• **Restoring Force:** The tension in the string acts as the restoring force, bringing the string back to its equilibrium position during oscillations.
 
• **Frequency and Wavelength:** The frequency of oscillation determines the pitch of the wave, while the wavelength determines its spatial characteristics.
 
• **Energy Transmission:** Waves in a string transfer mechanical energy from one point to another without any physical transfer of the string material.
 
• **Applications:** The principles of periodic oscillatory motion are utilized in musical instruments, scientific experiments, and engineering designs such as vibration testing.

questions.question: Which secret society founded by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar promoted armed revolution against the British rule?

• The organization aimed to overthrow British rule in India through **armed revolution** and militant activities.
 
• It was initially named **Mitra Mela** before being renamed Abhinav Bharat in 1906.
 
• Abhinav Bharat served as a platform for young revolutionaries to engage in nationalist activities, including **training for armed resistance**.
 
• The society drew inspiration from the Italian revolutionary Giuseppe Mazzini and his organization, **Young Italy**.

• Known as **Veer Savarkar**, he was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement.
 
• He authored the book **"The First War of Indian Independence"**, highlighting the 1857 revolt.
 
• He advocated the concept of **Hindutva** and was a key figure in shaping nationalist ideology.
 
• Imprisoned in the Cellular Jail (Kalapani) in Andaman and Nicobar Islands for his revolutionary activities.
 
 
 
• **Mitra Mela:**
 
 
• Founded by Savarkar in 1899, it was a precursor to Abhinav Bharat.
 
• Focused on fostering patriotism and organizing youth for revolutionary activities.
 
 
 
• **Giuseppe Mazzini:**
 
 
• An Italian revolutionary whose ideas influenced Savarkar.
 
• Founder of **Young Italy**, an organization advocating for Italian unification and independence.
 
 
 
• **Revolutionary Activities:**
 
 
• Abhinav Bharat members were involved in plotting attacks against British officials and institutions.
 
• It laid the groundwork for future revolutionary groups like the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Although disbanded by the 1910s, Abhinav Bharat inspired many freedom fighters in their struggle against British rule.
 
• Savarkar's vision of armed resistance influenced subsequent revolutionary movements in India.

It is the most common type of average, calculated by dividing the sum of values by the count of values (n).

questions.question: Three persons X, Y, and Z started a business with their shares in the ratio 3 : 4 : 10. After 6 months, Y withdrew his 50% share, while Z withdrew his 40% share 9 months prior to completion of the year. If the total profit at the end of the year is ₹23,400, find the share of Z (in ₹) in the profit.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Profit** = (Investment × Time).

X: (3 × 12) = 36.

Y: (4 × 6) + (2 × 6) = 24 + 12 = 36.

Z: (10 × 3) + (6 × 9) = 30 + 54 = 84.

Simplified Ratio (X : Y : Z) = 36 : 36 : 84 = **3 : 3 : 7**.

Total parts = 13. Given total profit = **₹23,400**.

Share of Z = (7 ÷ 13) × 23,400 = 7 × 1,800 = **₹12,600**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,600.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given → Initial investment ratio X : Y : Z = 3 : 4 : 10. Total duration = 12 months.
Formulas: Profit Share = Investment × Time Period | Total Profit = Sum of individual shares.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de9886e9b40cce5fb8497301108338797b30ee55cefc3c436a80a4c3f5b8877c.png] 
→ Let investments be 3k, 4k, and 10k.
→ **X's share** = 3k × 12 = 36k.
→ **Y's share** = (4k × 6) + (2k × 6) = 24k + 12k = 36k.
→ **Z's share**: Withdraws 40% (i.e., 4k) 9 months prior to completion. So, for the first 3 months investment was 10k, and for the remaining 9 months, it was 6k.
→ **Z's share** = (10k × 3) + (6k × 9) = 30k + 54k = 84k.
→ Ratio of shares = 36 : 36 : 84 = 3 : 3 : 7.
→ Sum of ratios = 3 + 3 + 7 = 13.
→ Value of 13 units = 23,400 ⇒ 1 unit = 1,800.
→ Z's share = 7 units × 1,800 = 12,600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,600.**

**__Additional Information__**

Partnership Ratio

When investments vary over different time periods, the profit is distributed in the ratio of the product of **Capital and Time**.

Withdrawals and Additions

Any change in capital must be accounted for by splitting the time period into segments where the **effective capital** remains constant.

• Article 43B of the Constitution of India focuses on the **promotion of cooperative societies** as a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• This provision emphasizes that the state shall endeavor to promote the formation and functioning of cooperative societies, ensuring their autonomy.
 
• Cooperative societies are recognized as instruments for socio-economic development, particularly in rural and agricultural sectors.
 
• The intent is to empower individuals and communities through collective efforts in areas such as agriculture, marketing, credit, and housing.

• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):** DPSPs are guidelines for the government to frame policies and laws aimed at achieving social and economic justice.
 
• **Cooperative Societies:** These are autonomous associations of persons united voluntarily to meet common economic, social, and cultural needs through jointly owned enterprises.

questions.question: A, B and C alone can do a piece of work in 5, 55 and 66 days, respectively. They all started the work together, but A left after 4 days. In how many days was the whole work completed?

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

questions.question: On simple interest, a certain sum of money amounts to ₹1,250 in 2 years and to ₹2,000 in 4 years. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest for 2 years (4 − 2 years) = ₹2,000 − ₹1,250 = ₹750.

**Principal (P)** = Amount after 2 years − Interest for 2 years = 1250 − 750 = ₹500.

**Rate (R)** = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100.

R = (375 ÷ 500) × 100 = 75%.

**∴ The correct answer is 75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount (A₁) = ₹1,250 at Time (T₁) = 2 years

Amount (A₂) = ₹2,000 at Time (T₂) = 4 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/990552967cd254d48bbb1f2936bf8e3b9ccd0239c0bd2a9bfac429ef3fe792f1.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + SI

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI for 2 years = A₂ − A₁

⇒ SI for 2 years = 2000 − 1250 = ₹750

⇒ Since SI is constant, SI for 1 year = 750 ÷ 2 = ₹375

⇒ Principal (P) = A₁ − SI for 2 years

⇒ P = 1250 − 750 = ₹500

⇒ Now, using SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100 for 1 year:

⇒ 375 = (500 × R × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 375 = 5 × R

⇒ R = 375 ÷ 5 = 75%

**∴ The correct answer is 75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI) Property

In Simple Interest, the interest earned remains **constant** for every equal time interval because it is always calculated on the original **Principal**.

Rate of Interest Formula

Rate (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T). For 1 year, R = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100.

Principal from Amount

Principal (P) = Amount (A) − Total Simple Interest (SI) accumulated over the given period.

• This limitation in sentencing authority is part of the tiered structure of the Indian judicial system, designed to distribute case handling based on the severity of offenses.

questions.question: The sum of two positive numbers x and y (where x > y) is 15 and their product is 36. Find the difference between the number x and y.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find two **factors** of 36 whose **sum** is 15.

The factors of 36 are: (1, 36), (2, 18), (3, 12), (4, 9), (6, 6).

Checking the sums: 1+36=37, 2+18=20, **3+12=15**, 4+9=13, 6+6=12.

The numbers are 12 and 3.

Difference = 12 − 3 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of numbers (x + y) = 15

Product of numbers (xy) = 36

Condition: x > y

**Formula Used:**

(x − y)² = (x + y)² − 4xy

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1e2451ad8f48eddb19666f73a4210204c91a80f7a7a022241303273ba225df5c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (x − y)² = (15)² − 4 × (36)

⇒ (x − y)² = 225 − 144

⇒ (x − y)² = 81

⇒ x − y = √81

⇒ x − y = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Sum and Difference

The relation between the square of the sum and the square of the difference is given by: (x + y)² − (x − y)² = 4xy.

Quadratic Equation Roots

If the sum (S) and product (P) of two numbers are known, the numbers are the roots of the quadratic equation: t² − St + P = 0.

Sum of Squares

The sum of the squares of the numbers can be found using: x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy. In this case, 225 − 72 = 153.</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **HCF** be **H**.

Numbers are 2H, 7H, and 13H.

Since 2, 7, and 13 are **prime numbers**, their LCM = 2 × 7 × 13 × H.

182 × H = 3094

H = 3094 ÷ 182 = 17.

**∴ The correct answer is 17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of numbers = 2 : 7 : 13

**LCM** of numbers = 3094

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dae4ce3c4987ea2c3ef90ff21143dffa6ed0f1f02052fb636aeb8f6a7f2fc8df.png] 

**Formula Used:**

LCM = HCF × (Product of ratios if ratios are co-prime)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the numbers be 2x, 7x, and 13x, where **x** is the **HCF**.

⇒ LCM(2x, 7x, 13x) = x × LCM(2, 7, 13)

⇒ Since 2, 7, and 13 are **co-prime**, their LCM = 2 × 7 × 13 = 182.

⇒ 182 × x = 3094

⇒ x = 3094 ÷ 182

⇒ x = 17

**∴ The correct answer is 17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF Relationship

For two numbers a and b, **a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**. This rule only applies to exactly two numbers.

HCF of Ratios

If the ratio of n numbers is a : b : c and their HCF is H, then the numbers are **aH, bH, and cH**.

Co-prime Numbers

If numbers are **co-prime** (HCF = 1), their LCM is simply the **product** of the numbers.</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply **Componendo and Dividendo** directly: (secθ − tanθ + secθ + tanθ) / (secθ − tanθ − secθ − tanθ) = (3 + 5) / (3 − 5).

⇒ 2secθ / (−2tanθ) = 8 / (−2)

⇒ secθ / tanθ = 4

⇒ (1/cosθ) / (sinθ/cosθ) = 4 ⇒ 1 / sinθ = 4

⇒ sinθ = 1/4

⇒ 2sinθ = 2 × (1/4) = 1/2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7742e44d32b550125d0dba05f43b1cfd37de5590991aa5d6482f51e20743053d.png] 

**Given:** (secθ − tanθ) / (secθ + tanθ) = 3 / 5

**Cross Multiplying:**

⇒ 5(secθ − tanθ) = 3(secθ + tanθ)

⇒ 5secθ − 5tanθ = 3secθ + 3tanθ

⇒ 5secθ − 3secθ = 3tanθ + 5tanθ

⇒ 2secθ = 8tanθ

⇒ secθ / tanθ = 8 / 2 = 4

⇒ (1 / cosθ) × (cosθ / sinθ) = 4

⇒ 1 / sinθ = 4

⇒ sinθ = 1 / 4

⇒ 2sinθ = 2 × (1/4) = 1/2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If a/b = c/d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This is very useful in simplifying trigonometric ratios.

Trigonometric Identities

Key identities: sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, hence (secθ − tanθ) = 1 / (secθ + tanθ).

Reciprocal Relations

secθ = 1/cosθ, cosecθ = 1/sinθ, and tanθ = sinθ/cosθ.</p

questions.question: What is the major reason behind higher road density in Kerala compared to Rajasthan?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kerala’s topography and population density** are key factors contributing to its higher road density compared to Rajasthan.
 
• Kerala has a **dense population of 859 persons per square kilometer** (Census 2011), requiring a robust road network for connectivity.
 
• The state’s **topography is dominated by undulating terrain and coastal plains**, which makes road construction more feasible than in Rajasthan's vast desert regions.
 
• Rajasthan, with a population density of **200 persons per square kilometer**, has vast arid and desert areas, making road construction challenging and less economically viable.
 
• Kerala’s high literacy rate and economic activities also demand better infrastructure, including roads, to support urbanization and trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Road density**: It is defined as the total length of roads per unit area or per unit population. Higher road density indicates better connectivity and infrastructure.
 
• **Topography**: The physical features of a region, such as plains, mountains, or deserts, significantly influence the feasibility and cost of road construction.
 
• **Population density**: Regions with higher population densities, like Kerala, require better connectivity to meet the transportation needs of the people.
 
• **Desert terrain in Rajasthan**: The Thar Desert covers a significant portion of Rajasthan, making road construction expensive and less practical in sparsely populated areas.
 
• **Economic factors**: Kerala’s economic activities, such as tourism, trade, and agriculture, necessitate a dense and well-maintained road network for accessibility and development.

questions.question: Find a single discount equal to three consecutive discounts of 20%, 13% and 20%.

Net discount for **20%** and **20%** = 20 + 20 − (20 × 20) ÷ 100 = **36%**.

Now, net discount for **36%** and **13%** = 36 + 13 − (36 × 13) ÷ 100.

⇒ 49 − 468 ÷ 100 = 49 − 4.68 = **44.32%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 44.32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Discounts are **d₁ = 20%**, **d₂ = 13%**, and **d₃ = 20%**.
Formulas: Successive discount = a + b − (ab ÷ 100) | SP = MP × (100 − d₁)% × (100 − d₂)% × ...
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38a11bcd1051052177f884a2edff03fa2ee51f5a49e754fef6dd8288e27d3a96.png] 
⇒ Let **Marked Price (MP)** = 100.
⇒ After 1st discount: 100 − 20% of 100 = **80**.
⇒ After 2nd discount: 80 − 13% of 80 = 80 − 10.4 = **69.6**.
⇒ After 3rd discount: 69.6 − 20% of 69.6 = 69.6 − 13.92 = **55.68**.
⇒ Single discount = MP − Final SP = 100 − 55.68 = **44.32%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 44.32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are allowed one after the other, they are called successive discounts. The order of applying these discounts does not change the final **Selling Price**.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. Formula: **Discount = MP − SP**.</p

questions.question: In the context of Local Area Networks (LANs), what is the primary purpose of a MAC (Media Access Control) address?

options.text: To define the physical layout and cabling of the network
To uniquely identify a network interface controller (NIC) at the data link layer
To specify the network protocol being used for communication
To provide a logical address for network routing

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To uniquely identify a network interface controller (NIC) at the data link layer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The MAC (Media Access Control) address is a **unique identifier assigned to a network interface controller (NIC)** for communication at the data link layer.
 
• It is a 48-bit address typically represented in hexadecimal format (e.g., 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E).
 
• The MAC address is globally unique, ensuring that each device's NIC can be distinctly identified on a network.
 
• It is essential for facilitating communication between devices within a Local Area Network (LAN).
 
• MAC addresses are assigned by the manufacturer and are often referred to as the "hardware address" or "physical address."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Data Link Layer:** This is the second layer in the OSI model, responsible for node-to-node data transfer and error detection.
 
• **IP Address vs. MAC Address:** While the MAC address identifies the physical device, the IP address is a logical address used for routing across networks.
 
• **Address Resolution Protocol (ARP):** ARP is used to map an IP address to a MAC address within a local network.
 
• **Types of MAC Addresses:** There are two types: **Unicast MAC** (for single devices) and **Multicast/Broadcast MAC** (for multiple devices or all devices on a network).
 
• **Role in Network Security:** MAC addresses can be used for access control mechanisms like MAC filtering to restrict devices on a network.

questions.question: If a : b :: b : c; c = 25a and b = 20, find the positive value of c
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **a : b :: b : c** ⇒ **b² = ac**.

Substitute **c = 25a** and **b = 20**.

(20)² = a × 25a ⇒ 400 = 25a².

a² = 16 ⇒ a = 4.

c = 25 × 4 = 100.

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/128568c582257f757ffe5978b2dd25ab9e0afeba5d0d6c73d638dcda1d10ead6.png] 

**Given:** b = 20, c = 25a

**Formula Used:** In a continued proportion a : b :: b : c, b² = ac

⇒ b² = a × c

⇒ (20)² = a × (25a)

⇒ 400 = 25a²

⇒ a² = 400 ÷ 25

⇒ a² = 16

⇒ a = √16 = 4

⇒ c = 25a = 25 × 4

⇒ c = 100

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: b : c, **b** is called the **mean proportional** between a and c, where b = √ac.

Third Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: b : c, **c** is called the **third proportional** to a and b, where c = b²/a.

Fourth Proportional

If four quantities a, b, c, d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then **d** is the **fourth proportional**, where d = (b × c) / a.</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **solid hemisphere**, the **total surface area** is always 3×π×r².

Given **radius (r)** = 16 cm.

TSA = 3 × π × (16)²

TSA = 3 × π × 256 = 768π cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 768π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius (r)** of the **solid hemisphere** = 16 cm.

**Formula Used:**

**Total Surface Area (TSA)** of a solid hemisphere = **Curved Surface Area** + **Area of base**

TSA = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8b5cc788be39044f92dc85e8362fd9f4d8c28bab60d90d59d73121a75bca881.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ TSA = 3 × π × (16)²

⇒ TSA = 3 × π × 256

⇒ TSA = 768π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 768π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere

The **CSA** of a hemisphere is exactly half of a sphere: CSA = 2πr².

Volume of Hemisphere

The space occupied by a hemisphere is calculated as Volume = (2/3)πr³.

Surface Area of a Sphere

For a full sphere, the total surface area is 4πr².</p

questions.question: The cost of 8 pens and 2 pencils is ₹96 and the cost of 4 pens and 7 pencils ₹72. The cost of 2 pens and 8 pencils is :
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Reduce the first condition: 8 Pens + 2 Pencils = ₹96 ⇒ 4 Pens + 1 Pencil = ₹48.

Compare this with the second condition: 4 Pens + 7 Pencils = ₹72.

The difference is 6 Pencils = 72 − 48 = ₹24 ⇒ **1 Pencil = ₹4**.

Calculate cost of 1 pen: 4 Pens = 48 − 4 = 44 ⇒ **1 Pen = ₹11**.

Cost of 2 pens and 8 pencils = 2 × 11 + 8 × 4 = 22 + 32 = 54.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 8 pens and 2 pencils = ₹96

Cost of 4 pens and 7 pencils = ₹72

**Formula Used:**

Simultaneous linear equations: ax + by = c

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b300058a5deb33a1a1c9eac72ed40b9ffb50c64d4d01f284b19316d2c6f3b957.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost of one **pen** be ₹x and one **pencil** be ₹y.

⇒ 8x + 2y = 96 — (Eq. 1)

⇒ 4x + 7y = 72 — (Eq. 2)

⇒ Divide (Eq. 1) by 2: 4x + y = 48 — (Eq. 3)

⇒ Subtract (Eq. 3) from (Eq. 2): (4x + 7y) − (4x + y) = 72 − 48

⇒ 6y = 24 ⇒ y = 4

⇒ Substitute y = 4 in (Eq. 3): 4x + 4 = 48 ⇒ 4x = 44 ⇒ x = 11

⇒ Cost of 2 pens and 8 pencils = 2x + 8y = 2(11) + 8(4)

⇒ Required Cost = 22 + 32 = 54

**∴ The correct answer is ₹54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Equations of the form ax + by + c = 0 where a and b are not zero are solved using elimination or substitution.

Method of Elimination

Multiplying one or both equations by suitable constants to make the coefficients of one variable equal, then adding or subtracting.

Consistency of Equations

A system has a unique solution if a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, which is the case for most item-cost problems.

questions.question: Which of the following is a National Park in Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ranthambore National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ranthambore National Park** is located in the Sawai Madhopur district of Rajasthan, India.
 
• It is one of the largest and most renowned national parks in Northern India.
 
• The park is famous for its significant population of Bengal tigers and provides a unique opportunity for tiger sightings in their natural habitat.
 
• Established in 1980, Ranthambore was declared a National Park under the Wildlife Protection Act.
 
• It is part of the larger Ranthambore Tiger Reserve, which is managed under India's Project Tiger initiative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Project Tiger:**

 
 
• Launched in 1973, Project Tiger is India's flagship conservation program aimed at preserving Bengal tigers and their habitats.
 
• The initiative involves habitat restoration, anti-poaching measures, and community participation.
 
• Ranthambore National Park is one of the key tiger reserves under this project.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Protection Act of 1972:**
 
 
• The act provides the legal framework for wildlife conservation and the establishment of National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries in India.
 
• Ranthambore National Park was designated under this act to protect its diverse flora and fauna.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Ranthambore:**
 
 
• The park spans an area of approximately 1,334 square kilometers, including the core and buffer zones.
 
• It features dry deciduous forests, open grasslands, and rocky terrains, making it a unique ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Key Attractions:**
 
 
• Besides tigers, the park is home to leopards, sambar deer, chital, nilgai, and sloth bears.
 
• Popular landmarks include the Ranthambore Fort, Padam Talao (lake), and ancient banyan trees.

questions.question: CMOS, often associated with storing system configuration, stands for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **CMOS** stands for **Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor**, a technology used in electronic circuits.
 
• It is widely used in modern digital integrated circuits, including microprocessors, microcontrollers, and other digital logic circuits.
 
• CMOS technology is characterized by its low power consumption, making it ideal for battery-operated devices.
 
• In computer systems, CMOS refers to a small amount of memory on the motherboard that stores BIOS settings, such as system time and hardware configurations.
 
• The CMOS battery powers this memory, ensuring the stored settings are retained even when the computer is turned off.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor (MOSFET):**

 
 
• CMOS technology relies on MOSFETs, which are transistors that use an electric field to control the flow of current.
 
• These transistors are used in pairs (p-type and n-type) in CMOS circuits to minimize power consumption.
 
 
 
• **Applications of CMOS:**
 
 
• Commonly found in digital cameras, smartphones, and other portable electronic devices.
 
• Essential for the production of energy-efficient processors and memory chips.
 
 
 
• **CMOS vs. TTL:**
 
 
• TTL (Transistor-Transistor Logic) was a widely-used technology before CMOS.
 
• CMOS is preferred over TTL for modern applications due to its lower power consumption and higher integration density.
 
 
 
• **CMOS Battery:**
 
 
• The CMOS battery, typically a CR2032 lithium cell, provides power to the CMOS memory chip to store BIOS settings.
 
• If the CMOS battery dies, the system may lose its time and hardware configuration settings, requiring manual reconfiguration.

questions.question: What is the name of the pillared hall at the front of a Hindu temple where devotees gather?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mandapa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Mandapa** is the pillared hall in front of the sanctum of a Hindu temple where devotees gather for prayers or rituals.
 
• It serves as a transitional space between the outer world and the sanctum (Garbhagriha) of the temple.
 
• Mandapas can be used for various religious and cultural activities, including congregations, dances, and discourses.
 
• Architecturally, the Mandapa is often ornately decorated with carvings and sculptures depicting mythological stories or deities.
 
• In larger temples, there may be multiple Mandapas, each serving a specific purpose, such as the Ardha-Mandapa (entrance porch) and Maha-Mandapa (great hall).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Garbhagriha:**

 
 
• The sanctum sanctorum of a Hindu temple where the main deity resides.
 
• It is the most sacred and innermost part of the temple.
 
• Access to the Garbhagriha is often restricted to priests or devotees during specific ceremonies.
 
 
 
• **Amalaka:**
 
 
• A stone disc, often ribbed, placed atop the temple shikhara (tower).
 
• It symbolizes the sun and is considered an important architectural and spiritual element in temple design.
 
 
 
• **Antarala:**
 
 
• A vestibule or intermediary space between the Garbhagriha and the Mandapa.
 
• It serves as a transitional area and provides visual as well as spiritual separation between the sanctum and the outer hall.
 
 
 
• **Temple Architecture:**
 
 
• Hindu temples are broadly categorized into Nagara (North Indian), Dravida (South Indian), and Vesara (mixed) styles.
 
• Each style has unique features, such as the shikhara in Nagara style and the gopuram in Dravida style.
 
 
 
• **Role of Mandapa in Rituals:**
 
 
• The Mandapa is often used for Vedic rituals, yajnas, weddings, and other religious ceremonies.
 
• It is also a space for devotees to sing bhajans (devotional songs) and meditate.

questions.question: Namita travels a certain distance at a speed of 88 km/hr and double the earlier distance at 16 km/hr. She then returns to the starting point through the same route. If her average speed for the entire journey is 33 km/hr, then what is her speed (in km/hr) for the return journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the first distance is **88 km**. Then the second distance is **176 km** (double). Return distance is **88 + 176 = 264 km**.

Total Distance = 88 + 176 + 264 = **528 km**.

Total Time = Total Distance ÷ Average Speed = 528 ÷ 33 = **16 hours**.

Time for first two parts = (88 ÷ 88) + (176 ÷ 16) = 1 + 11 = **12 hours**.

Return speed = Return Distance ÷ Remaining Time = 264 ÷ (16 − 12) = 264 ÷ 4 = **66 km/hr**.

**∴ The correct answer is 66 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a0338fe33cd9057c707bca99f8e3d7d1c30408158cc2296b264f185bf55eeee.png] 

**Given:** First speed = 88 km/hr, Second speed = 16 km/hr, Average speed = 33 km/hr.

**Formula:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Let distances be d, 2d, and 3d (return).

⇒ Total Distance = d + 2d + 3d = 6d

⇒ Total Time = (d/88) + (2d/16) + (3d/v) = (d/88) + (d/8) + (3d/v)

⇒ Average Speed = 6d ÷ [(d/88) + (11d/88) + (3d/v)] = 33

⇒ 6 ÷ [(12/88) + (3/v)] = 33

⇒ 6/33 = (3/22) + (3/v)

⇒ 2/11 = 3/22 + 3/v

⇒ 4/22 − 3/22 = 3/v

⇒ 1/22 = 3/v

⇒ v = 22 × 3 = 66 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 66 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If two equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, Average Speed = 2ab/(a+b). For three equal distances, Average Speed = 3abc/(ab+bc+ca).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is |v₁ − v₂|. In opposite directions, it is (v₁ + v₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Which enzyme, secreted by the chief cells of the stomach, is crucial for initiating the digestion of proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pepsinogen (converted to pepsin)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pepsinogen** is secreted by the chief cells of the stomach and is an inactive precursor enzyme (zymogen).
 
• It is converted into its active form, **pepsin**, in the presence of hydrochloric acid (HCl) secreted by the parietal cells.
 
• **Pepsin** is the primary enzyme responsible for breaking down proteins into smaller peptides in the acidic environment of the stomach.
 
• The activation of pepsinogen ensures that protein digestion begins in the stomach, which is essential for nutrient absorption in later stages of digestion.
 
• The stomach’s acidic pH (approximately 1.5–3.5) is crucial for the activation and function of pepsin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Cells:** Specialized cells located in the stomach lining that produce pepsinogen and gastric lipase.
 
• **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl):** Secreted by parietal cells in the stomach, HCl lowers the pH and facilitates the activation of pepsinogen into pepsin.
 
• **Protein Digestion:** Proteins are broken into smaller peptides by pepsin, and later into amino acids by enzymes in the small intestine like trypsin and chymotrypsin.
 
• **Trypsinogen vs. Pepsinogen:** Trypsinogen is secreted by the pancreas and activated into trypsin in the small intestine, while pepsinogen is activated into pepsin in the stomach.
 
• **Zymogen Activation:** Zymogens like pepsinogen are inactive forms of enzymes, activated under specific conditions to prevent self-digestion of the tissue that produces them.

questions.question: Not all regions in India equally benefited from the Green Revolution. Which of the following states was least impacted by the first phase of the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Orissa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India began in the 1960s and primarily focused on increasing agricultural productivity through the adoption of new technologies, such as high-yield variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and irrigation.
 
• The first phase of the Green Revolution significantly benefited regions with well-established irrigation systems and favorable agricultural conditions, such as Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Orissa, a state with limited irrigation facilities and a predominantly rain-fed agricultural system, was least impacted during the first phase of the Green Revolution.
 
• The focus of the Green Revolution on wheat cultivation further marginalized states like Orissa, where rice is the primary crop.
 
• The lack of infrastructure and technological advancements in Orissa during the initial phase hindered its ability to benefit from the Green Revolution compared to states in northern India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:** A period of agricultural transformation initiated in the 1960s to increase food production using modern techniques such as HYV seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation systems.
 
• **High-Yield Variety Seeds:** These seeds were central to the Green Revolution and provided significantly higher yields, especially for crops like wheat and rice.
 
• **Focus on Northern States:** The Green Revolution primarily benefited states like Punjab and Haryana due to their advanced irrigation systems and focus on wheat cultivation.
 
• **Limitations in Eastern India:** States like Orissa and Bihar faced challenges due to inadequate irrigation infrastructure and reliance on rain-fed agriculture, limiting the impact of the Green Revolution.
 
• **Second Phase of Green Revolution:** The later phase focused on extending the benefits to eastern and southern states, aiming to address disparities in agricultural development.

questions.question: Which of the following medicines discovered by Paul Ehrlich became the first successful treatment for syphilis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salvarsan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Salvarsan**, also known as Arsphenamine, was discovered by Paul Ehrlich in 1909 as the first effective treatment for syphilis.
 
• It was marketed as the "magic bullet" for its ability to target disease-causing pathogens without harming the host.
 
• Salvarsan is an organoarsenic compound, and its discovery marked a significant breakthrough in chemotherapy.
 
• The drug was revolutionary in reducing mortality and morbidity associated with syphilis, which was a major public health issue at the time.
 
• Paul Ehrlich's discovery laid the foundation for modern targeted drug therapy, influencing the development of antibiotics and other treatments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Syphilis:** A sexually transmitted bacterial infection caused by the spirochete Treponema pallidum. It progresses through primary, secondary, latent, and tertiary stages.
 
• **Paul Ehrlich:** A German physician and scientist known for his work in immunology, chemotherapy, and the discovery of Salvarsan.
 
• ** Ehrlich's concept of creating drugs that specifically target pathogens without damaging host cells, which became a cornerstone of pharmacology.
 
• Organometallic Compounds:** Salvarsan was one of the first organometallic compounds used in medicine, showcasing the potential of synthetic chemistry in drug discovery.
 
• **Antibiotics Development:** While Salvarsan was effective, the later discovery of Penicillin in 1928 by Alexander Fleming overshadowed it due to Penicillin's broader spectrum and fewer side effects.
